Fiber cutting module(s) Significant effort went into establishing a flexible cutting option for a range of fibers – glass, carbon and basalt. The design philosophy followed industry standard cutting methods. In general a rotary cutting mechanism was considered with one cutting roller, pressed against a contact (cot) roller and a pressure roller for uniform pressure as illustrated in Figure 2. Fiber rovings are fed from the feed pipes directly into the cot roller. This provides an uniform fiber feed and helps the fibers keep moving at the same speed as the blades. The approach was to directly feed the fiber rovings into the cutter, eliminating feed rollers. Figure 3 illustrates a schematic of glass and carbon fiber rovings being cut between the cutting roller and the contact (cot) roller. More consistent fiber lengths were realized by adjusting the spacing between blades. The blades were easy to access and reduced chance of fibers wrapping around rollers. A Finn & Framm design [11] illustrated in Figure 4 (bottom) was studied to evaluate the cutting mechanisms and the various adjustments. The design features (a) jets of air to blow fibers that may get stuck between the blades, and (b) pneumatic actuator to control pressure between the cot roller and the blades of the cutting roller.
